prompt.context_jp: 長年のライバル行との合併という知らせ___、行内の空気を一変させていたからだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 長年のライバル行との合併という知らせ___、行内の空気を一変させていたからだ。

feedback.correct_en: The merger news is being introduced as new information explaining why the atmosphere changed—が marks it as the newly-presented subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a continuing topic, but here the news is being introduced as the cause, not referenced as a known theme.

contrast_examples.jp: その知らせは本当だった。

prompt.context_jp: その日、舞と相馬の姿___本部ではなく、四谷支店の一室にあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その日、舞と相馬の姿___本部ではなく、四谷支店の一室にあった。

feedback.correct_en: は sets up contrastive topic: 'as for Mai and Souma's whereabouts, (not HQ but) the Yotsuya branch.' The 'not X but Y' structure needs contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply introduce them as new subjects, losing the contrastive 'not HQ, but...' nuance that structures the sentence.

prompt.context_jp: 部屋の中央には銀色のアタッシェケースが置かれ、子どもたちの視線___そこに釘付けになっている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 子どもたちの視線___そこに釘付けになっている。

feedback.correct_en: The case was just introduced with が; now 'the children's gaze' becomes the topic being described—は marks this topic continuation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce the gaze as new info, but the discourse has already moved to describing what happens around the case.

contrast_examples.en: There's a cat. The cat is white.

prompt.context_jp: 1万円札___1枚当たり約1ｇです。
prompt.prompt_jp: 1万円札___1枚当たり約1ｇです。

feedback.correct_en: This is a definitional statement about 10,000-yen bills as a topic—は introduces the topic 'as for 10,000-yen bills.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly single out the bill as new info; this sentence gives a general fact about them.

prompt.context_jp: ここでの説明役を引き受けたの___相馬で、かつて融資を担当していた経験を生かそうと、少し背筋を伸ばしている。
prompt.prompt_jp: ここでの説明役を引き受けたの___相馬で…

feedback.correct_en: The cleft structure 'the one who took the role was Souma' takes は: the nominalized clause is the topic, Souma is the comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-highlight the clause as new info; here the clause sets up what we're explaining about.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came is Tanaka.

prompt.context_jp: 私の元気の源___お客さまの笑顔です！
prompt.prompt_jp: 私の元気の源___お客さまの笑顔です！

feedback.correct_en: Sayoko introduces 'my source of energy' as the topic and declares what it is—は fits this X は Y identification pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would imply exhaustive 'it is specifically my source that is...', which doesn't fit this heartfelt declaration.

contrast_examples.en: Who's in charge? (asks for が answer)

prompt.context_jp: 舞の頭の中では、先ほどの小夜子の言葉___何度も繰り返されていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 先ほどの小夜子の言葉___何度も繰り返されていた。

feedback.correct_en: Sayoko's words are introduced as the thing that was repeating—new info in the described scene, marked with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the words as an already-established topic, but here they are the subject of a described event in Mai's mind.

prompt.context_jp: 現場の様子を伝えるアナウンサーの声___、いつになく硬かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: アナウンサーの声___、いつになく硬かった。

feedback.correct_en: The sentence comments on a known referent (the announcer's voice from context): 'as for the voice, it was tense.' Descriptive comment → は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the voice as new, but we're commenting on its quality, not announcing its presence.

prompt.context_jp: このニュースの犯人 どうやら うちの四谷支店でローン___断られていたらしいんだよ。
prompt.prompt_jp: このニュースの犯人 どうやら うちの四谷支店でローン___断られていたらしいんだよ。

feedback.correct_en: ローンを断られる is the passive construction 'to be refused a loan' — を marks the thing refused.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't fit because the suspect is the one being refused the loan; ローン is the object of refusal.

prompt.context_jp: 小夜子の顔___、昼間とは別人のように青ざめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 小夜子の顔___、昼間とは別人のように青ざめていた。

feedback.correct_en: Sayoko is an established character; the narrator comments on her face as topic: 'her face was pale.' → は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would treat the face as newly discovered subject, but we're describing a known person's state.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女の顔は青白かった。

prompt.context_jp: 自営業の上に 収入___不安定ですからね。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自営業の上に 収入___不安定ですからね。

feedback.correct_en: 自営業の上に... 収入も: 'on top of being self-employed, income is ALSO unstable'—も adds to the previous negative point.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply state that income is unstable without the cumulative 'on top of that' nuance 上に sets up.

contrast_examples.jp: 忙しい上に、疲れも溜まっている。
contrast_examples.en: On top of being busy, fatigue has also built up.

prompt.context_jp: その笑顔の端々に隠しきれない疲れ___にじんでいることに、舞は気づいていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隠しきれない疲れ___にじんでいることに、舞は気づいていた。

feedback.correct_en: Inside a こと-clause describing what Mai noticed, 疲れ is new information being observed—が marks it as the subject of the embedded perception.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside こと-clauses sounds odd when introducing new content observed; the fatigue is the discovered thing.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来たことに気づいた。

prompt.context_jp: 壁の時計の針の音だけ___、やけに大きく聞こえた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 壁の時計の針の音だけ___、やけに大きく聞こえた。

feedback.correct_en: 'Only the clock's ticking' is exhaustively identified as the sole sound heard—だけが marks this exhaustive listing.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would imply 'at least the ticking (as for that one)', but here the point is that ONLY that sound stood out.

prompt.context_jp: その前に立つの___、紀本の右腕として知られる昇仙峡玲子だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その前に立つの___、紀本の右腕として知られる昇仙峡玲子だった。

feedback.correct_en: Cleft: 'the one standing in front was Shosenkyo.' The nominalized clause is the topic, and は identifies.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively pick out the clause as new info, but the natural reading presents the relative clause as topic and reveals who it is.

contrast_examples.en: The one who spoke is the teacher.

prompt.context_jp: それこそ___、われわれの最優先事項だ。
prompt.prompt_jp: それこそ___、われわれの最優先事項だ。

feedback.correct_en: それこそが emphatically and exhaustively identifies 'THAT is precisely our top priority.' が carries the exhaustive emphasis こそ demands here.
feedback.incorrect_en: それこそは is ungrammatical/unnatural; こそ typically pairs with が for emphatic identification.

prompt.context_jp: 舟町ガス___四谷支店の大口取引先なんだよ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舟町ガス___四谷支店の大口取引先なんだよ。

feedback.correct_en: X は Y identification: 'as for Funamachi Gas, it's a major client of Yotsuya.' Already-mentioned entity as topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively pick out Funamachi Gas as 'the one that is...,' unnatural here since we're explaining what it is.

contrast_examples.jp: 田中さんが営業部長だ。

prompt.context_jp: 舟町ガスのメインバンク___当行ですが、産業中央とも取引があったのでは？
prompt.prompt_jp: 舟町ガスのメインバンク___当行ですが、産業中央とも取引があったのでは？

feedback.correct_en: Topic-comment with contrastive flavor: 'as for the main bank, it's us, BUT they also dealt with Chuo.' The が clause after shows contrast → は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively say 'OUR BANK is the main bank', clashing with the follow-up concession pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は医者ですが、母は教師です。
contrast_examples.en: Father is a doctor, but mother is a teacher.

prompt.context_jp: 地位なし 権力なし 怖いものなしの花咲舞が 今日もどこかで ___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 花咲舞が 今日もどこかで ___。

feedback.correct_en: お言葉を返す ('to talk back / contradict') is Mai's signature expression—she pushes back against her superiors.
feedback.incorrect_en: お返事をする just means 'to reply', and お言葉を頂く means 'to receive your words' (humble reception). Neither captures the pushback.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉を返すようですが…
contrast_examples.en: I hate to contradict you, but...

contrast_examples.jp: お返事お待ちしております。

prompt.context_jp: (To a visiting supervisor who apologized) 「お気遣い ___。」
prompt.prompt_jp: お気遣い ___。

feedback.correct_en: お気遣い恐れ入ります is a set business-polite response acknowledging someone's consideration with humility.
feedback.incorrect_en: ご苦労さま is used toward subordinates (rude up). 大丈夫です is too casual for this formal business exchange.

contrast_examples.jp: お手数おかけします。恐れ入ります。
contrast_examples.en: Sorry for the trouble. Much obliged.

contrast_examples.jp: ありがとうございます。

prompt.context_jp: 審査の結果 今回はご融資を___こととなりました。
prompt.prompt_jp: ご融資を___こととなりました。
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the humble business phrase for 'decline a loan.'

feedback.correct_en: 見送らせていただく is the standard softened business expression for declining/postponing—it sounds respectful and indirect.
feedback.incorrect_en: やめる and 断る are too blunt for banking register when refusing a customer's loan application.

contrast_examples.jp: 採用を見送らせていただきます。

prompt.context_jp: 手続きに問題はなかったようだし、とやかく言われる___はないだろう。
prompt.prompt_jp: とやかく言われる___はないだろう。

feedback.correct_en: 〜筋合いはない is a fixed expression meaning 'there's no reason/grounds for X to happen to us.' Souma asserts the bank doesn't deserve criticism.
feedback.incorrect_en: 立場 and 権利 would change the meaning; only 筋合い fits this 'no grounds to be criticized' idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: 文句を言われる筋合いはない。
contrast_examples.en: You have no right to complain to me.

prompt.context_jp: (Receiving a directive from a superior) 「___ます。」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the formal acknowledgment of a serious instruction.

feedback.correct_en: 肝に銘じる ('engrave on the liver') is the set phrase for solemnly taking a superior's words to heart.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options are not idiomatic; 肝に銘じる is specifically the formal expression here.

contrast_examples.jp: ご忠告を肝に銘じます。
contrast_examples.en: I'll take your advice deeply to heart.

prompt.context_jp: こういう時は 売り上げに___しないとな。
prompt.prompt_jp: 売り上げに___しないとな。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 売り上げに.

feedback.correct_en: 売り上げに貢献する ('contribute to sales') is the standard collocation Souma uses jokingly to mean they'll support Ken's shop.
feedback.incorrect_en: 参加する and 応援する don't take 売り上げに as an object naturally in this sense.

prompt.context_jp: 150億の融資を 他行に ___ なんて 支店長のクビが飛ぶレベルの大事件だ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 150億の融資を 他行に ___ なんて
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression for 'to be snatched away by.'

feedback.correct_en: 横取りする = snatching a deal that was yours. Standard banking usage for a rival bank stealing a client's loan.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持ち逃げ implies running off with money (embezzlement); 奪い取る is too physical/violent for finance.

contrast_examples.en: He ran off with the sales.

prompt.context_jp: 「融資を引き揚げるということでしょうか？」「___なご判断を期待します。」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___なご判断を期待します。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the business adjective for a 'wise' decision.

feedback.correct_en: 賢明なご判断 is a set business phrase pressuring the counterparty into the 'wise' (desired) decision.
feedback.incorrect_en: 丁寧 (polite/careful) and 正直 (honest) don't fit the implicit-pressure business idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: 賢明な選択をされますよう。
contrast_examples.en: We hope you'll make a wise choice.

contrast_examples.jp: 丁寧な対応をお願いします。

prompt.context_jp: Souma complains about being asked to guide a field trip.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Souma's grumble?

choices.text: まったく 社会科見学の案内まで 臨店の仕事なのか？
全部 社会科見学の案内さえ 臨店の仕事ですか？

feedback.correct_en: まったく as a grumble + 〜まで ('even this far') + rhetorical なのか？ perfectly matches Souma's exasperated, casual register.
feedback.incorrect_en: 全部 is wrong for 'even/of all things'; さえ is clumsy here; polite ですか clashes with his casual complaint.

contrast_examples.jp: まったく、休日出勤までするのか。

prompt.context_jp: Sayoko explaining her decision to quit and try something abroad.

choices.text: 挑戦するなら 今なのかなって。
挑戦すれば 今だと思ってって。

feedback.correct_en: 挑戦するなら今 ('if I'm going to try, now's the time') is a natural idiomatic reflection; 〜かなって softens it as personal musing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 挑戦すれば 今だ... mixes conditional with a declarative awkwardly and 思ってって is ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.en: If you're doing it, now's the time.

contrast_examples.jp: 行くなら早い方がいい。
contrast_examples.en: If you're going, sooner is better.

prompt.context_jp: Souma reviewing the loan file.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is more natural for 'I have no choice but to decline'?

choices.text: この内容じゃ 断らざるを得ないな。
この内容じゃ 断らないわけだな。

feedback.correct_en: 〜ざるを得ない expresses unavoidable obligation ('must, no choice'), fitting Souma's reluctant assessment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ないわけだ means 'that's why he doesn't,' explaining an existing fact, not expressing obligation to decline.

contrast_examples.en: I have no choice but to go.

prompt.context_jp: The bank clerk refusing to delay repayment for a struggling restaurant owner.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as a cold business refusal?

choices.text: 期日までにご返済いただけない場合は 所定の遅延損害金がかかります。
期日まで返せないなら 遅延損害金を払ってもらうことになります。

feedback.correct_en: The business-formal passive/humble construction ご返済いただけない場合は with 所定の fits a bank counter perfectly—polite yet unyielding.
feedback.incorrect_en: The B version is too conversational for a bank window; 返せないなら and 払ってもらう sound confrontational, not procedural.

contrast_examples.jp: ご入金いただけない場合は…
払ってくれないと困る。
contrast_examples.en: We're in trouble if you don't pay. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: Mai justifying going to the rival bank for information.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line is more natural for Mai's reasoning?

choices.text: どうせ合併するなら 敵じゃありませんよ。
どうせでも合併したら 敵じゃないんですよ。

feedback.correct_en: どうせ〜なら ('since we're going to X anyway') is a natural idiomatic framing. The direct じゃありませんよ sounds like Mai's confident style.
feedback.incorrect_en: どうせでも is not a standard combination; 合併したら changes the nuance and the whole line feels unnatural.

contrast_examples.jp: どうせやるなら本気でやろう。
contrast_examples.en: If we're doing it anyway, let's go all in.
